subject: Materials Science
title: Self-Assembly: Nature's Nanofabrication
description: A micro-lesson that makes Self-Assembly: Nature's Nanofabrication usable.

hook.text: Drop a solution on a surface and molecules arrange themselves into perfect monolayers — no tools, no templates.

buildup.text: Self-assembly uses intermolecular forces — van der Waals, hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic effects — to organize.

discovery.text: Block copolymers spontaneously form nanoscale patterns — spheres, cylinders, or lamellae depending on composition.

twist.text: Self-assembly is cheap and parallel — but controlling defects and long-range order remains a major challenge.

climax.text: DNA origami folds single DNA strands into precise 3D nanostructures — self-assembly with atomic programmability.

punchline.text: Let molecules build themselves — nature's own assembly is the cheapest.

quiz.question: What drives molecular self-assembly?
options: External mechanical forces pushing molecules into place
Intermolecular forces like van der Waals and hydrogen bonds
